title: Which model is best for Ai game dev?
author: Spare-Ad-1024
selftext: My brain is buzzing with excitement as I build my dream game: a Titanic RPG with the sinking as the climactic finale. I’ve been using ChatGPT Sol 6.1 and it’s doing a decent job. Timon and Pumbaa diet but hey, progress is progress.  Is Claude a better option or perhaps another model? DeepSeek isn’t quite up to scratch yet.

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: Opus 5.5 and it’s not even close

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: The new Fable is better but it destroys your usage. Also if you have the funds, a 100 account with Open (for Astra) really helps find bugs that Opus won't find.

replies.author: AMGsoon
replies.body:
Fable is okay too. Just use sub agents. I run Fable and then it uses Haiku and Sonnet. Its great for improving details and introducing new ideas/more complex systems.

Opus as base model is unbeatable though.

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: Sure. And vise versa. After extensive usage of both, for our workflow, Claude is vastly superior.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: Agree, I meant Astra to go along with Claude being the workhorse.

replies.author: vriemeister
replies.body: What about all the art and 3d work? Seems like other tools do that better and claude is best used to integrate them.

replies.author: piperspalace
replies.body:
Im sure this is the case just wondering about things like qwen 4, open code and local models.
Or is Claude so far ahead that i shouldn't even bother with game dev. My reason for asking about qwen 4 us because it kniws creation kit 2 and papyrus 2.

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: I use Qwen 4 paired with a 3090 and development is really really slow. A Qwen task that would take 4 hours takes 10 min on Opus 5.5 high. Its such a big different that the doesnt make it worth the time to use Qwen. For us of course.

replies.author: piperspalace
replies.body: Are you using open hands or something for the APIs or did you just have both? I do have a 5090 had QFN running at 130-170 tokens a second. So its not bad. But thinking does take a while. Plus fixing code.

replies.author: celikogeday
replies.body: I tried a simple game-dev test on my own hardware: build a playable Tetris game for the browser. GPT‑6 Astra on Medium produced a working version. Qwen3.5‑9B Q6\_K gave me HTML with a JavaScript syntax error, Gemma 4 12B IT QAT finished in 2m 37s but failed 12 out of 20 checks, and Qwen3.8‑27B IQ4\_XS still hadn’t returned any code after 20 minutes. That was enough for me to stick with Codex when I need a playable prototype from scratch.

comments.author: RetroFuturistMan
comments.body: As someone who uses Claude, Codex and Gemini. Claude. And it's not close. I migrated my entire workflow to claude using Codex and Gemini as satellite agents for simple tasks or asset production. Gemini is a competent modeler. Codex a competent code monkey. Claude just has much better whole project vision.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body: Claude is number 1 and i dont see it changing anytime soon. Opus 5.5 is goated and incredibly versatile depending on your budget, Sonnet 5.5 is a great workforce as long as you have clear scope for it and have it being “guided” by Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.2, Haiku same as Sonnet but for tedious bulk tasks, naming, searching and similar and now the big boss arrived which is Fable 5.2 and i cant compliment it enough. Yes, its token hungry but if you have Max and especially if you have the Ultra plan its a terrific model to have in the workflow for harder and critical tasks and especially visual related ones.

I've been working on my projects for a few months now and I've made more progress in the last 30 days since switching than I have since i started

comments.body: Yeah,  Opus 5.5 for new development, if the task is known and repetitive Sol 6.1 on high can get the work done

comments.author: jawni
comments.body: Everyone saying Opus 5.5 but this shit can change in the blink of an eye. Seeing as the jump between tiers is usually $20 to $100, if you tend to run out of usage it makes a ton of sense just to get the $20 sub for both ChatGPT and Claude.

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: Worth saying the best model usually depends on the job more than the brand. For code and keeping a bigger project coherent, Claude-style models with a decent project file describing your architecture tend to hold up better over long sessions. For design docs, quest writing and dialogue, the model matters less than giving it a clear tone guide and a few example lines. A Titanic RPG with a big sinking finale is a state-heavy game (flooding, timers, who is where), so it's worth trying to have the model write that as a small state machine first and testing it in isolation. Whatever you pick, keep each request small and commit after every working change so you can roll back when it goes sideways.

comments.author: je386
comments.body: I used claude sonnet 4.5 for a while, now claude haiku 5.5 is as good as sonnet 4.5 was, and haiku is super cheap. Most tasks are less than 30 cents, and I have a task for a feature.

comments.body: lol the thread is basically an opus fan club. which, fair for code. but dont pick off vibes, take one real chunk of your game, like the save system or the flooding timer, give sol and claude the exact same prompt and see which one you have to babysit less. thats your answer for YOUR project. also whoever said grab both $20 plans for a month instead of one $100 is onto something

comments.author: kingkongy
comments.body: Each have what they are good at. Quarterbacking the development is for sure Opus. Sometimes switching to Fable for complex tasks works well, but generally stay on Opus for efficiency.

comments.author: celikogeday
comments.body:
In my own game dev projects, Claude usually gets closer to what I had in mind. It asks more questions before making assumptions, which is great when a design decision matters. For smaller details, though, I like that Codex can make a reasonable call and keep going without asking me about every little thing. Claude also costs me more and burns through my token budget faster.



I use Sol 6.1 on High for about 95% of the coding and implementation. Once Sol finishes a feature, I switch to Astra on High for testing and a deeper review. Sometimes I give Astra the whole project and ask it to look for bugs and edge cases I missed while building it. That split has worked well for me.
